mechanism_narrative: A positive growth in real GDP (GDPC1) over the prior quarter signals robust economic expansion, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth is positive over the prior quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 3.5% in the prior month, it indicates an aggressive monetary easing stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical rate cuts in 2020-2023 correlated with 5-day SPX gains
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which fuels consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day return is negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 330), the Federal Reserve's policy response typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Inflation above 330 in 2022-2023 led to 60-day SPX losses
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 330.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity, which is a leading indicator of economic health and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day return is negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO rises.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.5% in the prior month, it signals economic weakness and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment above 4.5% in 2020-2021 coincided with SPX declines
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in the real estate sector, which reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL (inflation trend) over the prior month typically leads to expectations of tighter monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises.
